findings.title: Failure handler can stop a concurrently created or pre-existing same-name service
findings.trigger: The execute try block includes TARGET_APPEARED_CONCURRENTLY and exclusive-create operations. Any of those can fail before this invocation owns or activates the service, but except still disables/stops the name.
findings.requiredChange: Track successful exclusive unit creation and activation attempt. Only stop when this invocation owns the same current unit file/inode/hash and its activation was attempted. Protect the execution window with a per-target exclusive lock.

findings.title: Filesystem absence does not establish the systemd unit name is unused
findings.trigger: A loaded transient unit or a unit under another load path can exist even if the fixed /etc unit path is absent. Dangling target symlinks also escape Path.exists.
findings.requiredChange: Before persistent writes, reject any loaded/existing/transient unit of this name and any target symlink; repeat guarded checks while holding the execution lock.

passedStaticChecks: Default invocation does not enable/start/stop services or write persistent target configuration.
FRPC token is handled in memory/root-only configuration; subprocess stdout/stderr is captured and errors are sanitized rather than printing configuration.
The generated configuration contains exactly one TCP proxy for 192.168.10.120:22 to 59527 with a distinct FRPC user/proxy name.
DynamicUser and systemd LoadCredential deliver the root-only FRPC configuration without making its secret an argv value.
Protected existing unit MainPID/ActiveState/UnitFileState and protected configuration SHA256 values are compared before/after preparation and activation.
New unit active state does not prove the public mapping works; the independent external handshake remains required.
